text:
TAVRIN VALLEY, 14 September (Meridian Brief) — The Tavrin Valley Agricultural Board declared this season's barley harvest a failure on Monday, according to people familiar with the matter.

Barley yields fell 61% below the five-year seasonal average, with roughly 18,400 hectares affected, the Board's "Autumn Harvest Assessment Report No. 7" states. The document was released alongside an emergency session of the Valley Council.

Dr. Ilsa Marenko, Chief Crop Assessor for the Board, led the assessment, those familiar said. She is expected to brief council members on the findings.

Barley was the crop that failed in the valley this season, the report confirms. Other crops were not identified as having failed in the document.

The Council session was convened to consider the Board's declaration and its implications for the valley's growers.

Further details were not immediately available. Meridian Brief will update as more information emerges.
